description: jest-testing is targeted against a complaint about trust in the test run's own report — never coverage, an option, or the skill's own vocabulary — with unit-testing (a coverage-questions reading of the same complaint) and quality-assurance (a was-this-really-verified reading of it) sitting in the peer set as competing, plausible-looking picks. The outcome factors check that the fix actually declares which files Jest instruments, rather than merely turning `--coverage` on — a naive answer that would make the very module the owner is worried about disappear from the report instead of appearing as uncovered — and that it measures with the runner's own `v8` instrumentation, which jest-testing prefers for a project whose transform (`next/jest`'s SWC, not Babel) is this one's shape. `jest.config.cjs` declares neither option today, so a control run has nothing local to copy.

task.prompt: `npm test` prints a row of green ticks and I have stopped trusting it. Before I rewrite the locale matching under `shared/` I want to be able to run something that tells me how much of the code in there the tests actually exercise — and I want it honest about the files no test touches at all, because those are exactly the ones I am worried about. Make it something I can run again later rather than a one-off you paste into chat. Do not add any new tests yet; I want to see the gap first.

factors.description: The complaint names no coverage percentage, no config option, and no runner — only that the green ticks are no longer trusted — so an agent that reaches for jest-testing here is finding it from the problem, with unit-testing (which names "coverage questions" in its own description) and quality-assurance (which asks whether a change was really verified) sitting right there as competing, plausible-looking picks; the actual answer is the runner's own machinery, which is jest-testing's territory.

This is the defect in the naive answer, and jest-testing states it as a MUST: with `--coverage` alone Jest reports only on files the tests loaded, so `shared/resolve-translation.ts` — the module the owner is actually worried about — does not appear as uncovered, it disappears and quietly raises the reported percentage. The fix has to declare `collectCoverageFrom` so an untouched file stays visible in the report; `jest.config.cjs` declares no coverage option today, so there is nothing local to copy.

jest-testing prefers `v8` coverage instrumentation over Babel's own in a project whose transform is not Babel — and `jest.config.cjs` wraps `next/jest`, which transforms with SWC. The fix has to set `coverageProvider` to `v8` rather than leave the default; this asserts adherence to what the skill teaches for a project of this shape, stated here so a reader can disagree with the expectation without reading the script.
